Context / standards / procedures

Operating Packs keep the domain in view.

A reusable, file-based body of context and instructions that tells an agent how work should be performed within a particular domain, system, or project environment.

Markdown-firstSource and status stay visibleContext is scoped to the work

What belongs here

Operating Packs own contextual operating knowledge.

They may contain or reference AGENTS.md, architecture, conventions, testing, security, accessibility, domain guidance, workflows, references, and validation instructions. Persona Library catalogs the pack and its relationships; the actual Markdown files may live in this repository, another repository, a project workspace, or remain planned.

Known packs

Search the catalog, then inspect a pack’s purpose, applicability, source, entrypoint, status, context types, and scoped relationships. A planned or unavailable source stays clearly labeled.

0 packs

Read the status honestly

A catalog relationship is useful only when its source and confidence are legible. The pack’s lifecycle status and source availability answer different questions.

Canonical reusable

Use when a stable pack has a supported scope and source. Its rules can be reused by relevant work while remaining distinct from Skills and Playbooks.

Project-specific

Use for local repository or project rules. Keep them local until evidence and review justify a broader pack; a Work Order can track the compilation.

Planned or unavailable

A reference may be known without its files being present. Record repository, intended path, entrypoint, and availability without pretending the pack can be loaded.

What an Operating Pack does not do

It provides context; it does not execute.

Skills own reusable expertise and judgment. Tools act under scope and permissions. Playbooks coordinate stages and outcomes. A pack can guide those layers, but it does not install files, grant access, call a Tool, run a workflow, or turn a project convention into a universal Skill automatically.
